programme: FOXO1 induces PPARGC1A (PGC-1α), which coactivates RXRA-containing nuclear receptor complexes to drive mitochondrial biogenesis and antioxidant gene expression (PPARGC1A targets include TFAM, NRF1, COX4I1, COX5B, CYCS, MFN2, SOD2; FOXO1 targets include PPARGC1A itself, BCL2L1, BAX, FOXO3) — a redox/mitochondrial-biogenesis checkpoint in stressed epithelium.
role_in_a: In COPD, this axis is the epithelial response to cigarette-smoke-induced mitochondrial injury: FOXO1 is directly implicated in smoke-driven senescence and fibrosis in lung fibroblasts and in bronchial biomarker studies, PPARGC1A/PPAR signaling opposes smoke-induced mitochondrial apoptosis in alveolar type II cells, and RXRA drives PLA2G2A-mediated airway remodeling in COPD models — together placing the axis as a mitochondrial-quality-control node whose failure contributes to epithelial injury.
role_in_b: In psoriasis, the same nuclear-receptor/coactivator logic is expected to govern keratinocyte proliferation-differentiation balance and redox homeostasis: RXR is the receptor class targeted therapeutically by retinoids (e.g. acitretin) to normalize keratinocyte differentiation, and FOXO1/PGC-1α-driven mitochondrial and antioxidant programs are the generic mechanism by which a chronically cytokine-stressed epidermis would need to manage oxidative load — but none of this is documented for this factor set in the material retrieved here.
shared_axis: Bronchial/alveolar epithelium and epidermis are both barrier tissues subjected to chronic external stress (smoke oxidants vs. cytokine-driven inflammatory stress), and the FOXO1-PPARGC1A-RXRA node is a conserved epithelial checkpoint for mitochondrial biogenesis and antioxidant defense that either tissue would need to engage under sustained insult.
reasoning: The COPD side of this axis is independently grounded by multiple disease-specific papers for all three carrying factors, and their moderate, comparably-sized counts (57/104 each) are consistent with a real but not dominant signal. The psoriasis side has no Open Targets association and no retrieved paper for any of the three factors, so the cross-disease link rests on the generic epithelial-stress argument and on the well-known clinical use of RXR ligands in psoriasis rather than on anything retrieved for this pair — hence supported, not established, and moderate rather than strong.
support: PMID 41164273 — FOXO1/FOXO3 contribution to COPD examined directly; PMID 40498253 — FOXO1 drives cigarette-smoke-induced senescence and fibrosis in lung fibroblasts; PMID 40612794 — FOXO1 linked to mitochondrial dysfunction/cell death biomarkers in COPD; PMID 40245976 — FOXO1-adjacent pathway modulation reduces inflammation/oxidative stress in a COPD-relevant model; PMID 42361513 — PPARGC1A-linked Hes1 overexpression blocks smoke-induced mitochondrial apoptosis in AT2 cells; PMID 40655182 — PPAR signaling pathway reviewed as central to COPD diagnosis/treatment; PMID 40950286 — RXRA-mediated PLA2G2A transcription drives airway remodeling in COPD; PMID 38372090 — RXRA-PLA2G2A inhibition improves a COPD delirium/ER-stress model. No PMID above bears on psoriasis for any of these three factors.
how_to_falsify: In parallel air-liquid-interface bronchial epithelial cultures (smoke-exposed) and IL-17/IL-22-stimulated keratinocyte cultures, knock down PPARGC1A and RXRA and measure the mitochondrial-biogenesis/antioxidant target set (TFAM, NRF1, COX4I1, COX5B, SOD2). If loss of this axis fails to blunt these targets concordantly in both epithelial systems, or if psoriatic-lesion transcriptomes show no coordinated shift in FOXO1/PPARGC1A/RXRA target genes relative to healthy skin, the shared-axis claim is falsified.
caveats: 104 patient-group comparisons come from only 4 independent cohort pairs, so the count is inflated by within-cohort correlation rather than 104 independent replications. All three carrying factors sit in Open Targets' COPD association list but have no recorded Psoriasis association at all — the psoriasis half of this account is inference, not retrieved evidence. The exclusion lists contain no tissue-generic epithelial master regulator that this account substitutes for, and none of the single-view factors (e.g. FOXP2, NR1D2) were folded in, so the module is not propped up by a one-off subgroup finding. Several other concordant factors (CEBPG, HIVEP1, NR3C2, SF1, RBPJ, KLF6, NRG1, KAT5, EGR1) were left out of the carrying set because they do not sit in this specific coactivator relationship, not because they were disqualified.
